**What:** forward `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (or resolve gh's config dir another way) on the non-network `run` path that the gh auth probe uses.

**Why:** `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` IS in the forwarded allowlist — but that allowlist only applies to `runNetwork` (`:106-108` feeds `networkEnvironment`, applied at `:195` behind `if network`). `resolveGitHubCLI` uses plain `run`, and the comment at `:96-97` justifies the split by saying gh "carries its own token." **Context:** consistent across every gh probe today, so it is a coherent design rather than an oversight — but the design predates knowing that an empty config reads as a confident logout. **What:** stop `VCSToolVersionCache` caching a `.notInstalled` verdict that came from a PATH miss, or re-probe once the interactive-shell PATH probe lands.

**Why:** `ShellEnvironment.path()` (`:285-287`) returns the probed PATH if the probe has finished and the deterministic floor otherwise — silently, with no readiness signal. The floor covers Homebrew, but NOT a version-manager shim dir, Nix, MacPorts, or a bare `export PATH` in `.zshrc`. `refreshVCSToolReport` is called from `apply(projects)` (`AppStore.swift:2492`), i.e. right after load, and the probe is kicked off detached at `WorkroomApp.swift:43` with nothing joining it — so the tool probe can genuinely run on floor-only PATH. A miss gives exit 127, which `status:149` maps to `.notInstalled`, `warnings(hasJJProject:):111-112` turns into a "jj isn't installed" warning, and `VCSToolVersionCache` (`:183-206`) then caches for the whole process — `cached` is cleared only by `reset()`, which is tests-only. Note `.unknown` is deliberately ignored by `warnings` (`:107-108`), so a signalled or timed-out probe already fails safe; only the 127 path is sticky.

**Pros:** removes a wrong, unfixable-without-restart warning for anyone whose jj lives in a shim or Nix profile. **Cons:** it is a race whose window is small, git effectively cannot miss (`/usr/bin/git` ships with the CLT and is always on the floor), and the honest fix is a readiness signal on `ShellEnvironment`, which is a bigger change than it looks.

**Context:** same root as the shipped psql PATH work — the floor is deterministic, the probe is best-effort enrichment, and nothing exposes "has the probe landed?" Simplest fix: do not cache `.notInstalled` (only `.ok`, `.belowFloor`, `.unknown`), so a later call re-probes against the enriched PATH. **Depends on:** nothing; entirely separate from the gh work.

Recommendation: A — verified through four files, but it is a different subsystem with a different root cause, and the "don't cache the negative" fix deserves to be judged against a readiness-signal alternative rather than picked by default.

# Fix the false, sticky "GitHub CLI not signed in" in the PR panel

## Context

The PR panel intermittently claims `GitHub CLI not signed in`, then recovers on its own about a
minute later. Root cause confirmed by measurement.

A superseded status sweep (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:60`) or a workroom switched mid-probe
(`:118`) cancels the task awaiting `gh auth status --active --json hosts`. The runner's `onCancel`
SIGKILLs the child (`StatusCommandRunner.swift:301-307`), but its `withCheckedContinuation` is
**non-throwing**, so `terminationHandler` (`:252-268`) still resumes with `exitCode: 9` (SIGKILL —
measured; signal numbers stay well below `commandNotFound: 127`), `timedOut: false`, and
empty-or-half-written stdout.

That walks the classifier (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:434-444`): not 127, not timed out, no
parseable JSON, so it falls to `r.ok ? .available : .notAuthenticated` → **`.notAuthenticated`**.

`refreshGitHubCLI` (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:103-113`) then writes that verdict **and stamps
`ghStatusCheckedAt`** with no `Task.isCancelled` check. It is the only mutation in that file buried
*behind* an await, so the callers' guards at `:86`/`:144` come too late. The stamp is the sticky
half: the TTL gate at `:105-109` early-returns for every unforced caller, so for 60s every lane that
would have healed the value is suppressed by the value's own stamp, while `:87`/`:145` gate off the
whole CI/PR probe. Only the manual Refresh button (`ChangesPanel.swift:143`, the sole `force: true`
path) escapes early. The verdict lives on the process-wide `ProjectStore.shared.githubCLIStatus`, so
one window's cancelled probe paints and suppresses every other window's panel.

```
  THE POISONED-CACHE LOOP  (what makes a 200ms blip last 60 seconds)

  lane B starts ──cancel()──► lane A's `gh auth status` child
                                      │ SIGKILL
                                      ▼
                        CommandResult(exitCode: 9, timedOut: false, stdout: "")
                                      │
                     classifyGitHubCLI │ not 127 · not timedOut · no JSON
                                      ▼
                             .notAuthenticated          ◄── a lie: nothing was learned
                                      │
                  refreshGitHubCLI:112 │ writes value AND stamps TTL   (no isCancelled guard)
                                      ▼
                 ProjectStore.shared ──┬──► PR panel: "GitHub CLI not signed in"   (every window)
                                       └──► ghStatusCheckedAt = now
                                                     │
                     ┌───────────────────────────────┘
                     ▼
              TTL gate :105-109 ──► every unforced caller returns EARLY for 60s
                     │                    ▲
```

# PR1 — the fix (small, independently revertable)

## 1. `CommandResult.signaled` — `Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift`

- `CommandResult` (`:8-20`) gains `let signaled: Bool` plus an **explicit init** with
  `signaled: Bool = false` last. Do **not** write `let signaled: Bool = false`: Swift drops a
  `let` with an initial value from the synthesized memberwise init entirely, and the only compile
  error is the one line that tries to set it. All ~63 `CommandResult(` sites use labelled args, so a
  trailing defaulted parameter keeps every one compiling; no consumer compares whole values, so the
  widened synthesized `==` breaks nothing.
- `terminationHandler` (`:262-267`): `signaled: finished.terminationReason == .uncaughtSignal`.
- **Trap to comment loudly:** the timeout path calls `proc.terminate()` (`:239`) — SIGTERM — so a
  timed-out child has `timedOut == true` **AND** `signaled == true`. Every consumer must therefore
  test `timedOut` first. `markTimedOut()` already precedes `terminate()` at `:237-240`, so the
  ordering is safe as long as classifiers respect it.

## 2. "No news" becomes representable — `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`

`.available` is not "no news", it is a positive claim that gh works — and writing it over a correct
`.notAuthenticated` erases a true warning with a false silence. The codebase already has the right
word two functions down (`ghPreflight`'s `.keepPrior`). So:

```swift
enum GHAuthProbe: Equatable {
  case verdict(GitHubCLIStatus)
  case keepPrior          // the probe told us nothing — killed, crashed, timed out
}

static func classifyGitHubCLI(_ r: CommandResult) -> GHAuthProbe {
  if r.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .verdict(.notInstalled) }
  if r.timedOut { return .keepPrior }                                  // MUST precede signaled
  if let s = classifyGitHubCLIJSON(r.stdout) { return .verdict(s) }     // a complete verdict wins
  if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }                                  // no verdict ⇒ no evidence
  return r.ok ? .verdict(.available) : .verdict(.notAuthenticated)
}
```

`resolveGitHubCLI()` returns `GHAuthProbe`. Two orderings are load-bearing and both get a test:
`timedOut` before `signaled` (a timeout is also a signal), and the JSON parse before `signaled` (a
child that emitted a complete 401 and was *then* killed has genuinely told us the token is bad).

This also corrects the pre-existing `.available`-on-timeout lie at `:436`.

`ghPreflight` (`:495-504`) gets `if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }` immediately after its own
`timedOut` check. Not a live bug — all four apply sites (`:153`, `:156`, `:166`, `:169`) are guarded
— so comment it as braces to those guards' belt.

## 3. Nothing from a cancelled or uninformative probe is published — `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`

```swift
let probe = await resolver.resolveGitHubCLI()
if Task.isCancelled { return }                            // a cancelled probe holds no fact
guard case .verdict(let status) = probe else { return }   // .keepPrior: no write, NO STAMP
githubCLIStatus = status
ghStatusCheckedAt = Date()
```

Bail entirely rather than write-value-but-skip-stamp: a cancelled probe's value is garbage too.
Comment why, because the instinct that produced the bug ("a machine-global fact is worth recording
even from a cancelled task") is defensible and wrong.

`.keepPrior` deliberately does **not** stamp, so the next lane re-probes instead of trusting a
non-answer for the full TTL. That is the structural repair; the asymmetric TTL in PR2 is then only
about re-confirming a *real* `.notAuthenticated` sooner.

## 4. `VCSWriting.swift` — stop printing a signal number as an exit code

`:1099` and `:1197` end with `.other("\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)")` when stderr is empty, so a
signalled `git push` renders the literal `git exited 15` in the failure sheet — verbatim the dialog
`a64e4269` claims to have stopped, because that fix never reached this runner. Insert immediately
before each fallback, so any real stderr still classifies:

```swift
let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other("\(tool) was interrupted") }
return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
```

`.other` already carries Retry as its recovery, which is correct for an interrupted write, so no new
enum case. **Rebase note:** `VCSWriting.swift` has uncommitted changes in the working tree.

## 5. Prose corrections (part of the change, not follow-ups)

- `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:440-442` claims the fallback covers "pre-2.57 gh without `--json`".
  Measured false — an old gh *rejects* the flag (exit 1, empty stdout, `unknown flag: --json`).
  Rewrite to say what the fallback actually covers, and point at PR2 for the real handling.
- `TODOS.md:202-207` defers the `withTimeout` cancellation fix on the grounds that "every call site
  already checks `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result … so state stays correct". This bug
  is the counterexample, and the consequence was a wrong published value, not wasted CPU. Correct the
  rationale; **keep the deferral** — that entry's mechanism (`withTimeout`) is genuinely unrelated to
  this one (`runner.run`'s non-throwing continuation).

# PR2 — hardening (all approved, lands after PR1)

## 6. `GitHubCLIStatus.tooOld` + actionable copy

gh < 2.57 rejects `--json`, so a signed-in user currently reads as permanently logged out. Detect it
and say so:

- `static func rejectedUnknownFlag(_ r: CommandResult) -> Bool` — non-zero exit, no parseable JSON,
  stderr contains **`unknown flag`** matched *generically*, not the `--json` literal: `--active` has
  the same floor and gh reports whichever flag it parses first.
- New case in the classifier, ahead of the final fallback: `.verdict(.tooOld)`.
- Extract the panel copy out of the view body into a pure function and switch on all four states:

```swift
static func ghWarningCopy(for status: GitHubCLIStatus)
  -> (title: String, body: String, showsInstallLink: Bool)
```

`.tooOld` → "GitHub CLI too old" / "Workroom needs gh 2.57 or newer — run `brew upgrade gh`." and
**no** install link. `PullRequestPanel.swift:36`, `:42-44`, `:48` stop being ternaries.
`ChangesPanel.swift:220`/`:240` already gate on `== .available`, so they need no edit.

Rejected: re-running plain `gh auth status`. Two classifiers to keep in sync — the drift risk the
code warns about at `:485-488` — and it reinstates the #86 network-blip flap.

## 7. `Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift` — instance-owned single-flight

Today the TTL read (`:105-109`) sits before the await and the stamp (`:112`) after it, `AppStore` is
per-window (`WorkroomApp.swift:103`) while the verdict is a shared singleton, and two windows both
probe with last-write-wins. Fix it with an **instance**, not a static — `AppStore.swift:793-795`
already guarantees tests get a fresh `ProjectStore`, and `make app-test` runs parallel, so static
state would let one test's fake runner serve another's probe while `reset()` cannot stop an in-flight
task repopulating the cache.

```
  GitHubAuthCache  (one per ProjectStore — isolation comes free)

   caller(force: false) ─┐
   caller(force: false) ─┼─► fresh within TTL? ──yes──► return cached verdict
   caller(force: false) ─┘            │no
                                      ▼
                          in-flight non-forced probe? ──yes──► JOIN it
                                      │no
                                      ▼
                        ┌── cache-owned Task { resolver.resolveGitHubCLI() }
                        │   (NOT the caller's task: a cancelled waiter no
                        │    longer SIGKILLs the gh child, so this path stops
                        │    producing killed results at all)
                        ▼
              .verdict(x) ─► store x + stamp monotonic instant
              .keepPrior  ─► keep previous verdict, DO NOT stamp

   caller(force: true) ──► never joins a non-forced flight; starts a NEW probe
                           (concurrent forced callers join each other)
```

Contracts, each written down and each tested:
- **Ownership.** The cache is the *sole* TTL owner. `ProjectStore.ghStatusCheckedAt` and its
  `AppStore` proxy (`:296-299`) are **deleted**; `ProjectStore.githubCLIStatus` remains as the
  SwiftUI-observable mirror.
- **Cancellation.** The probe runs in a cache-owned task, so it survives a cancelled waiter and
  yields a real verdict. The `Task.isCancelled` guard and `signaled` still earn their keep — OS
  kills, crashes, sleep/wake signals, and every other `CommandResult` consumer.
- **Force.** `force: true` starts a new probe rather than joining a non-forced flight, so Refresh
  really refreshes.
- **Clock.** Staleness is measured on a **monotonic** clock (`ContinuousClock`), not `Date`, so a
  backward wall-clock adjustment cannot extend the cache indefinitely. TTLs are init parameters, so
  the negative-TTL test runs in 50ms instead of sleeping. (The local/CI lanes keep their `Date`
  stamps; only this cache changes.)

## 8. Asymmetric TTL — 60s normal, 10s for `.notAuthenticated`

`.notAuthenticated` is both the alarming answer and the sink every ambiguous result used to fall
into, and it gates the entire PR/CI lane, so it is re-confirmed quickly. A genuine logout still warns
on the **first** probe; only caching shortens. Implement as an init parameter so the value is a
one-line tuning change — and **re-judge 10s once `.keepPrior` is in**, since not stamping an
ambiguous probe removes most of what this was compensating for. Flat rather than exponential matches
`applyCIStatus:567-568`, which already records backoff as a future refinement.

## 9. `UITestFixture.ghStatus` seam

Adding a flag alone changes nothing: `refreshGitHubCLI` hard-returns in fixture mode at `:104`. The
seeded status must be applied during fixture load **and** on manual reseeding, and must not be
overwritten by the optimistic `.available` default (`ProjectStore.swift:35`). That gap is why no
XCUITest can drive any gh state today.

# Lane C — independent, parallel with PR1

## 10. `VCSToolVersionCache` must not cache a `.notInstalled`

`ShellEnvironment.path()` (`:285-287`) silently returns the floor until the interactive-shell probe
lands, and the probe is fired detached at `WorkroomApp.swift:43` with nothing joining it while
`refreshVCSToolReport` runs from `apply(projects)` (`AppStore.swift:2492`). The floor covers
Homebrew but not a version-manager shim dir, Nix, or MacPorts — so a PATH miss gives 127, `status:149`
maps it to `.notInstalled`, `warnings:111-112` shows "jj isn't installed", and the cache pins it for
the whole process (`cached` is cleared only by the tests-only `reset()`).

Fix: cache only `.ok`, `.belowFloor`, and `.unknown`. A `.notInstalled` verdict re-probes on the next
call, against the by-then-enriched PATH. Fails in the safe direction — at worst a redundant
`--version`. (`.unknown` already fails safe: `warnings:107-108` ignores it.)

# Fix the false, sticky "GitHub CLI not signed in" in the PR panel

## Context

The PR panel intermittently claims `GitHub CLI not signed in`, then recovers on its own about a
minute later. Root cause confirmed by measurement.

A superseded status sweep (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:60`) or a workroom switched mid-probe
(`:118`) cancels the task awaiting `gh auth status --active --json hosts`. The runner's `onCancel`
SIGKILLs the child (`StatusCommandRunner.swift:301-307`), but its `withCheckedContinuation` is
**non-throwing**, so `terminationHandler` (`:252-268`) still resumes with `exitCode: 9` (SIGKILL —
measured; signal numbers stay well below `commandNotFound: 127`), `timedOut: false`, and
empty-or-half-written stdout.

That walks the classifier (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:434-444`): not 127, not timed out, no
parseable JSON, so it falls to `r.ok ? .available : .notAuthenticated` → **`.notAuthenticated`**.

`refreshGitHubCLI` (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:103-113`) then writes that verdict **and stamps
`ghStatusCheckedAt`** with no `Task.isCancelled` check. It is the only mutation in that file buried
*behind* an await, so the callers' guards at `:86`/`:144` come too late. The stamp is the sticky
half: the TTL gate at `:105-109` early-returns for every unforced caller, so for 60s every lane that
would have healed the value is suppressed by the value's own stamp, while `:87`/`:145` gate off the
whole CI/PR probe. Only the manual Refresh button (`ChangesPanel.swift:143`, the sole `force: true`
path) escapes early. The verdict lives on the process-wide `ProjectStore.shared.githubCLIStatus`, so
one window's cancelled probe paints and suppresses every other window's panel.

```
  THE POISONED-CACHE LOOP  (what makes a 200ms blip last 60 seconds)

  lane B starts ──cancel()──► lane A's `gh auth status` child
                                      │ SIGKILL
                                      ▼
                        CommandResult(exitCode: 9, timedOut: false, stdout: "")
                                      │
                     classifyGitHubCLI │ not 127 · not timedOut · no JSON
                                      ▼
                             .notAuthenticated          ◄── a lie: nothing was learned
                                      │
                  refreshGitHubCLI:112 │ writes value AND stamps TTL   (no isCancelled guard)
                                      ▼
                 ProjectStore.shared ──┬──► PR panel: "GitHub CLI not signed in"   (every window)
                                       └──► ghStatusCheckedAt = now
                                                     │
                     ┌───────────────────────────────┘
                     ▼
              TTL gate :105-109 ──► every unforced caller returns EARLY for 60s
                     │                    ▲
                     └────────────────────┘  the wrong value suppresses its own repair
                          escape hatch: ONLY the Refresh button (force: true)
```

Measured against real gh 2.97.0: the `--json` payload goes to **stdout** and exit is **0** in all
three genuine states (signed in `state:"success"`; bad token `state:"error"` + `HTTP 401 ... Bad
credentials`; no config `{"hosts":{}}`). So the exit-code fallback is never reached in normal
operation — everything landing there is ambiguous by construction. A keyring/transport failure
produces a *populated* host entry with a non-401 error, already routed away by
`isGitHubAuthFailure` (`:479-482`).

Outcome wanted: an uninformative probe must never publish anything, and an ambiguous one must never
be trusted for a minute.

# PR1 — the fix (small, independently revertable)

## 1. `CommandResult.signaled` — `Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift`

- `CommandResult` (`:8-20`) gains `let signaled: Bool` plus an **explicit init** with
  `signaled: Bool = false` last. Do **not** write `let signaled: Bool = false`: Swift drops a
  `let` with an initial value from the synthesized memberwise init entirely, and the only compile
  error is the one line that tries to set it. All ~63 `CommandResult(` sites use labelled args, so a
  trailing defaulted parameter keeps every one compiling; no consumer compares whole values, so the
  widened synthesized `==` breaks nothing.
- `terminationHandler` (`:262-267`): `signaled: finished.terminationReason == .uncaughtSignal`.
- **Trap to comment loudly:** the timeout path calls `proc.terminate()` (`:239`) — SIGTERM — so a
  timed-out child has `timedOut == true` **AND** `signaled == true`. Every consumer must therefore
  test `timedOut` first. `markTimedOut()` already precedes `terminate()` at `:237-240`, so the
  ordering is safe as long as classifiers respect it.

## 2. "No news" becomes representable — `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`

`.available` is not "no news", it is a positive claim that gh works — and writing it over a correct
`.notAuthenticated` erases a true warning with a false silence. The codebase already has the right
word two functions down (`ghPreflight`'s `.keepPrior`). So:

```swift
enum GHAuthProbe: Equatable {
  case verdict(GitHubCLIStatus)
  case keepPrior          // the probe told us nothing — killed, crashed, timed out
}

static func classifyGitHubCLI(_ r: CommandResult) -> GHAuthProbe {
  if r.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .verdict(.notInstalled) }
  if r.timedOut { return .keepPrior }                                  // MUST precede signaled
  if let s = classifyGitHubCLIJSON(r.stdout) { return .verdict(s) }     // a complete verdict wins
  if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }                                  // no verdict ⇒ no evidence
  return r.ok ? .verdict(.available) : .verdict(.notAuthenticated)
}
```

`resolveGitHubCLI()` returns `GHAuthProbe`. Two orderings are load-bearing and both get a test:
`timedOut` before `signaled` (a timeout is also a signal), and the JSON parse before `signaled` (a
child that emitted a complete 401 and was *then* killed has genuinely told us the token is bad).

This also corrects the pre-existing `.available`-on-timeout lie at `:436`.

`ghPreflight` (`:495-504`) gets `if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }` immediately after its own
`timedOut` check. Not a live bug — all four apply sites (`:153`, `:156`, `:166`, `:169`) are guarded
— so comment it as braces to those guards' belt.

## 3. Nothing from a cancelled or uninformative probe is published — `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`

```swift
let probe = await resolver.resolveGitHubCLI()
if Task.isCancelled { return }                            // a cancelled probe holds no fact
guard case .verdict(let status) = probe else { return }   // .keepPrior: no write, NO STAMP
githubCLIStatus = status
ghStatusCheckedAt = Date()
```

Bail entirely rather than write-value-but-skip-stamp: a cancelled probe's value is garbage too.
Comment why, because the instinct that produced the bug ("a machine-global fact is worth recording
even from a cancelled task") is defensible and wrong.

`.keepPrior` deliberately does **not** stamp, so the next lane re-probes instead of trusting a
non-answer for the full TTL. That is the structural repair; the asymmetric TTL in PR2 is then only
about re-confirming a *real* `.notAuthenticated` sooner.

## 4. `VCSWriting.swift` — stop printing a signal number as an exit code

`:1099` and `:1197` end with `.other("\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)")` when stderr is empty, so a
signalled `git push` renders the literal `git exited 15` in the failure sheet — verbatim the dialog
`a64e4269` claims to have stopped, because that fix never reached this runner. Insert immediately
before each fallback, so any real stderr still classifies:

```swift
let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other("\(tool) was interrupted") }
return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
```

`.other` already carries Retry as its recovery, which is correct for an interrupted write, so no new
enum case. **Rebase note:** `VCSWriting.swift` has uncommitted changes in the working tree.

## 5. Prose corrections (part of the change, not follow-ups)

- `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:440-442` claims the fallback covers "pre-2.57 gh without `--json`".
  Measured false — an old gh *rejects* the flag (exit 1, empty stdout, `unknown flag: --json`).
  Rewrite to say what the fallback actually covers, and point at PR2 for the real handling.
- `TODOS.md:202-207` defers the `withTimeout` cancellation fix on the grounds that "every call site
  already checks `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result … so state stays correct". This bug
  is the counterexample, and the consequence was a wrong published value, not wasted CPU. Correct the
  rationale; **keep the deferral** — that entry's mechanism (`withTimeout`) is genuinely unrelated to
  this one (`runner.run`'s non-throwing continuation).

# PR2 — hardening (all approved, lands after PR1)

## 6. `GitHubCLIStatus.tooOld` + actionable copy

gh < 2.57 rejects `--json`, so a signed-in user currently reads as permanently logged out. Detect it
and say so:

- `static func rejectedUnknownFlag(_ r: CommandResult) -> Bool` — non-zero exit, no parseable JSON,
  stderr contains **`unknown flag`** matched *generically*, not the `--json` literal: `--active` has
  the same floor and gh reports whichever flag it parses first.
- New case in the classifier, ahead of the final fallback: `.verdict(.tooOld)`.
- Extract the panel copy out of the view body into a pure function and switch on all four states:

```swift
static func ghWarningCopy(for status: GitHubCLIStatus)
  -> (title: String, body: String, showsInstallLink: Bool)
```

`.tooOld` → "GitHub CLI too old" / "Workroom needs gh 2.57 or newer — run `brew upgrade gh`." and
**no** install link. `PullRequestPanel.swift:36`, `:42-44`, `:48` stop being ternaries.
`ChangesPanel.swift:220`/`:240` already gate on `== .available`, so they need no edit.

Rejected: re-running plain `gh auth status`. Two classifiers to keep in sync — the drift risk the
code warns about at `:485-488` — and it reinstates the #86 network-blip flap.

## 7. `Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift` — instance-owned single-flight

Today the TTL read (`:105-109`) sits before the await and the stamp (`:112`) after it, `AppStore` is
per-window (`WorkroomApp.swift:103`) while the verdict is a shared singleton, and two windows both
probe with last-write-wins. Fix it with an **instance**, not a static — `AppStore.swift:793-795`
already guarantees tests get a fresh `ProjectStore`, and `make app-test` runs parallel, so static
state would let one test's fake runner serve another's probe while `reset()` cannot stop an in-flight
task repopulating the cache.

```
  GitHubAuthCache  (one per ProjectStore — isolation comes free)

   caller(force: false) ─┐
   caller(force: false) ─┼─► fresh within TTL? ──yes──► return cached verdict
   caller(force: false) ─┘            │no
                                      ▼
                          in-flight non-forced probe? ──yes──► JOIN it
                                      │no
                                      ▼
                        ┌── cache-owned Task { resolver.resolveGitHubCLI() }
                        │   (NOT the caller's task: a cancelled waiter no
                        │    longer SIGKILLs the gh child, so this path stops
                        │    producing killed results at all)
                        ▼
              .verdict(x) ─► store x + stamp monotonic instant
              .keepPrior  ─► keep previous verdict, DO NOT stamp

   caller(force: true) ──► never joins a non-forced flight; starts a NEW probe
                           (concurrent forced callers join each other)
```

Contracts, each written down and each tested:
- **Ownership.** The cache is the *sole* TTL owner. `ProjectStore.ghStatusCheckedAt` and its
  `AppStore` proxy (`:296-299`) are **deleted**; `ProjectStore.githubCLIStatus` remains as the
  SwiftUI-observable mirror.
- **Cancellation.** The probe runs in a cache-owned task, so it survives a cancelled waiter and
  yields a real verdict. The `Task.isCancelled` guard and `signaled` still earn their keep — OS
  kills, crashes, sleep/wake signals, and every other `CommandResult` consumer.
- **Force.** `force: true` starts a new probe rather than joining a non-forced flight, so Refresh
  really refreshes.
- **Clock.** Staleness is measured on a **monotonic** clock (`ContinuousClock`), not `Date`, so a
  backward wall-clock adjustment cannot extend the cache indefinitely. TTLs are init parameters, so
  the negative-TTL test runs in 50ms instead of sleeping. (The local/CI lanes keep their `Date`
  stamps; only this cache changes.)

## 8. Asymmetric TTL — 60s normal, 10s for `.notAuthenticated`

`.notAuthenticated` is both the alarming answer and the sink every ambiguous result used to fall
into, and it gates the entire PR/CI lane, so it is re-confirmed quickly. A genuine logout still warns
on the **first** probe; only caching shortens. Implement as an init parameter so the value is a
one-line tuning change — and **re-judge 10s once `.keepPrior` is in**, since not stamping an
ambiguous probe removes most of what this was compensating for. Flat rather than exponential matches
`applyCIStatus:567-568`, which already records backoff as a future refinement.

## 9. `UITestFixture.ghStatus` seam

Adding a flag alone changes nothing: `refreshGitHubCLI` hard-returns in fixture mode at `:104`. The
seeded status must be applied during fixture load **and** on manual reseeding, and must not be
overwritten by the optimistic `.available` default (`ProjectStore.swift:35`). That gap is why no
XCUITest can drive any gh state today.

# Lane C — independent, parallel with PR1

## 10. `VCSToolVersionCache` must not cache a `.notInstalled`

`ShellEnvironment.path()` (`:285-287`) silently returns the floor until the interactive-shell probe
lands, and the probe is fired detached at `WorkroomApp.swift:43` with nothing joining it while
`refreshVCSToolReport` runs from `apply(projects)` (`AppStore.swift:2492`). The floor covers
Homebrew but not a version-manager shim dir, Nix, or MacPorts — so a PATH miss gives 127, `status:149`
maps it to `.notInstalled`, `warnings:111-112` shows "jj isn't installed", and the cache pins it for
the whole process (`cached` is cleared only by the tests-only `reset()`).

Fix: cache only `.ok`, `.belowFloor`, and `.unknown`. A `.notInstalled` verdict re-probes on the next
call, against the by-then-enriched PATH. Fails in the safe direction — at worst a redundant
`--version`. (`.unknown` already fails safe: `warnings:107-108` ignores it.)

| New codepath | Realistic production failure | Test? | Handled? | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `refreshGitHubCLI` after cancel | superseded sweep during a slow probe | yes (critical regression) | yes — bail before write | nothing changes (correct) |

# Fix the false, sticky "GitHub CLI not signed in" in the PR panel

## Context

The PR panel intermittently claims `GitHub CLI not signed in`, then recovers on its own about a
minute later. Root cause confirmed by measurement.

A superseded status sweep (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:60`) or a workroom switched mid-probe
(`:118`) cancels the task awaiting `gh auth status --active --json hosts`. The runner's `onCancel`
SIGKILLs the child (`StatusCommandRunner.swift:301-307`), but its `withCheckedContinuation` is
**non-throwing**, so `terminationHandler` (`:252-268`) still resumes with `exitCode: 9` (SIGKILL —
measured; signal numbers stay well below `commandNotFound: 127`), `timedOut: false`, and
empty-or-half-written stdout.

That walks the classifier (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:434-444`): not 127, not timed out, no
parseable JSON, so it falls to `r.ok ? .available : .notAuthenticated` → **`.notAuthenticated`**.

`refreshGitHubCLI` (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:103-113`) then writes that verdict **and stamps
`ghStatusCheckedAt`** with no `Task.isCancelled` check. It is the only mutation in that file buried
*behind* an await, so the callers' guards at `:86`/`:144` come too late. The stamp is the sticky
half: the TTL gate at `:105-109` early-returns for every unforced caller, so for 60s every lane that
would have healed the value is suppressed by the value's own stamp, while `:87`/`:145` gate off the
whole CI/PR probe. Only the manual Refresh button (`ChangesPanel.swift:143`, the sole `force: true`
path) escapes early. The verdict lives on the process-wide `ProjectStore.shared.githubCLIStatus`, so
one window's cancelled probe paints and suppresses every other window's panel.

```
  THE POISONED-CACHE LOOP  (what makes a 200ms blip last 60 seconds)

  lane B starts ──cancel()──► lane A's `gh auth status` child
                                      │ SIGKILL
                                      ▼
                        CommandResult(exitCode: 9, timedOut: false, stdout: "")
                                      │
                     classifyGitHubCLI │ not 127 · not timedOut · no JSON
                                      ▼
                             .notAuthenticated          ◄── a lie: nothing was learned
                                      │
                  refreshGitHubCLI:112 │ writes value AND stamps TTL   (no isCancelled guard)
                                      ▼
                 ProjectStore.shared ──┬──► PR panel: "GitHub CLI not signed in"   (every window)
                                       └──► ghStatusCheckedAt = now
                                                     │
                     ┌───────────────────────────────┘
                     ▼
              TTL gate :105-109 ──► every unforced caller returns EARLY for 60s
                     │                    ▲
                     └────────────────────┘  the wrong value suppresses its own repair
                          escape hatch: ONLY the Refresh button (force: true)
```

Measured against real gh 2.97.0: the `--json` payload goes to **stdout** and exit is **0** in all
three genuine states (signed in `state:"success"`; bad token `state:"error"` + `HTTP 401 ... Bad
credentials`; no config `{"hosts":{}}`). So the exit-code fallback is never reached in normal
operation — everything landing there is ambiguous by construction. A keyring/transport failure
produces a *populated* host entry with a non-401 error, already routed away by
`isGitHubAuthFailure` (`:479-482`).

Outcome wanted: an uninformative probe must never publish anything, and an ambiguous one must never
be trusted for a minute.

# PR1 — the fix (small, independently revertable)

## 1. `CommandResult.signaled` — `Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift`

- `CommandResult` (`:8-20`) gains `let signaled: Bool` plus an **explicit init** with
  `signaled: Bool = false` last. Do **not** write `let signaled: Bool = false`: Swift drops a
  `let` with an initial value from the synthesized memberwise init entirely, and the only compile
  error is the one line that tries to set it. All ~63 `CommandResult(` sites use labelled args, so a
  trailing defaulted parameter keeps every one compiling; no consumer compares whole values, so the
  widened synthesized `==` breaks nothing.
- `terminationHandler` (`:262-267`): `signaled: finished.terminationReason == .uncaughtSignal`.
- **Trap to comment loudly:** the timeout path calls `proc.terminate()` (`:239`) — SIGTERM — so a
  timed-out child has `timedOut == true` **AND** `signaled == true`. Every consumer must therefore
  test `timedOut` first. `markTimedOut()` already precedes `terminate()` at `:237-240`, so the
  ordering is safe as long as classifiers respect it.

## 2. "No news" becomes representable — `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`

`.available` is not "no news", it is a positive claim that gh works — and writing it over a correct
`.notAuthenticated` erases a true warning with a false silence. The codebase already has the right
word two functions down (`ghPreflight`'s `.keepPrior`). So:

```swift
enum GHAuthProbe: Equatable {
  case verdict(GitHubCLIStatus)
  case keepPrior          // the probe told us nothing — killed, crashed, timed out
}

static func classifyGitHubCLI(_ r: CommandResult) -> GHAuthProbe {
  if r.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .verdict(.notInstalled) }
  if r.timedOut { return .keepPrior }                                  // MUST precede signaled
  if let s = classifyGitHubCLIJSON(r.stdout) { return .verdict(s) }     // a complete verdict wins
  if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }                                  // no verdict ⇒ no evidence
  return r.ok ? .verdict(.available) : .verdict(.notAuthenticated)
}
```

`resolveGitHubCLI()` returns `GHAuthProbe`. Two orderings are load-bearing and both get a test:
`timedOut` before `signaled` (a timeout is also a signal), and the JSON parse before `signaled` (a
child that emitted a complete 401 and was *then* killed has genuinely told us the token is bad).

This also corrects the pre-existing `.available`-on-timeout lie at `:436`.

`ghPreflight` (`:495-504`) gets `if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }` immediately after its own
`timedOut` check. Not a live bug — all four apply sites (`:153`, `:156`, `:166`, `:169`) are guarded
— so comment it as braces to those guards' belt.

## 3. Nothing from a cancelled or uninformative probe is published — `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`

```swift
let probe = await resolver.resolveGitHubCLI()
if Task.isCancelled { return }                            // a cancelled probe holds no fact
guard case .verdict(let status) = probe else { return }   // .keepPrior: no write, NO STAMP
githubCLIStatus = status
ghStatusCheckedAt = Date()
```

Bail entirely rather than write-value-but-skip-stamp: a cancelled probe's value is garbage too.
Comment why, because the instinct that produced the bug ("a machine-global fact is worth recording
even from a cancelled task") is defensible and wrong.

`.keepPrior` deliberately does **not** stamp, so the next lane re-probes instead of trusting a
non-answer for the full TTL. That is the structural repair; the asymmetric TTL in PR2 is then only
about re-confirming a *real* `.notAuthenticated` sooner.

## 4. `VCSWriting.swift` — stop printing a signal number as an exit code

`:1099` and `:1197` end with `.other("\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)")` when stderr is empty, so a
signalled `git push` renders the literal `git exited 15` in the failure sheet — verbatim the dialog
`a64e4269` claims to have stopped, because that fix never reached this runner. Insert immediately
before each fallback, so any real stderr still classifies:

```swift
let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other("\(tool) was interrupted") }
return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
```

`.other` already carries Retry as its recovery, which is correct for an interrupted write, so no new
enum case. **Rebase note:** `VCSWriting.swift` has uncommitted changes in the working tree.

## 7. `Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift` — instance-owned single-flight

Today the TTL read (`:105-109`) sits before the await and the stamp (`:112`) after it, `AppStore` is
per-window (`WorkroomApp.swift:103`) while the verdict is a shared singleton, and two windows both
probe with last-write-wins. Fix it with an **instance**, not a static — `AppStore.swift:793-795`
already guarantees tests get a fresh `ProjectStore`, and `make app-test` runs parallel, so static
state would let one test's fake runner serve another's probe while `reset()` cannot stop an in-flight
task repopulating the cache.

```
  GitHubAuthCache  (one per ProjectStore — isolation comes free)

   caller(force: false) ─┐
   caller(force: false) ─┼─► fresh within TTL? ──yes──► return cached verdict
   caller(force: false) ─┘            │no
                                      ▼
                          in-flight non-forced probe? ──yes──► JOIN it
                                      │no
                                      ▼
                        ┌── cache-owned Task { resolver.resolveGitHubCLI() }
                        │   (NOT the caller's task: a cancelled waiter no
                        │    longer SIGKILLs the gh child, so this path stops
                        │    producing killed results at all)
                        ▼
              .verdict(x) ─► store x + stamp monotonic instant
              .keepPrior  ─► keep previous verdict, DO NOT stamp

   caller(force: true) ──► never joins a non-forced flight; starts a NEW probe
                           (concurrent forced callers join each other)
```

Contracts, each written down and each tested:
- **Ownership.** The cache is the *sole* TTL owner. `ProjectStore.ghStatusCheckedAt` and its
  `AppStore` proxy (`:296-299`) are **deleted**; `ProjectStore.githubCLIStatus` remains as the
  SwiftUI-observable mirror.
- **Cancellation.** The probe runs in a cache-owned task, so it survives a cancelled waiter and
  yields a real verdict. The `Task.isCancelled` guard and `signaled` still earn their keep — OS
  kills, crashes, sleep/wake signals, and every other `CommandResult` consumer.
- **Force.** `force: true` starts a new probe rather than joining a non-forced flight, so Refresh
  really refreshes.
- **Clock.** Staleness is measured on a **monotonic** clock (`ContinuousClock`), not `Date`, so a
  backward wall-clock adjustment cannot extend the cache indefinitely. TTLs are init parameters, so
  the negative-TTL test runs in 50ms instead of sleeping. (The local/CI lanes keep their `Date`
  stamps; only this cache changes.)

## 8. Asymmetric TTL — 60s normal, 10s for `.notAuthenticated`

`.notAuthenticated` is both the alarming answer and the sink every ambiguous result used to fall
into, and it gates the entire PR/CI lane, so it is re-confirmed quickly. A genuine logout still warns
on the **first** probe; only caching shortens. Implement as an init parameter so the value is a
one-line tuning change — and **re-judge 10s once `.keepPrior` is in**, since not stamping an
ambiguous probe removes most of what this was compensating for. Flat rather than exponential matches
`applyCIStatus:567-568`, which already records backoff as a future refinement.

Adding a flag alone changes nothing: `refreshGitHubCLI` hard-returns in fixture mode at `:104`. The
seeded status must be applied during fixture load **and** on manual reseeding, and must not be

500	      let root = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String: Any],

input.new_string:
**Why:** Wastes CPU/time re-running a probe nobody wants anymore, and — post the jj-snapshot-gate
fix — adds unnecessary extra contention pressure on `JJSnapshotGate` (an unwanted, already-abandoned
caller still occupies a project's queue slot for up to its full timeout). This is a
responsiveness/efficiency gap, not a data-integrity one, because the call sites in this seam do
check `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result (`runLocalSweep`'s
`if Task.isCancelled { break }`, etc.).

**Corrected 2026-08-05 — do NOT re-read this entry as "the convention protects us".** This used to
say *every* call site already checks, so state stays correct. That was false, and the counterexample
shipped: `refreshGitHubCLI` mutated `githubCLIStatus` **inside** an awaited function, where the
callers' own guards (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:86`/`:144`) run too late to help. A cancelled
probe's SIGKILLed `gh` still returned through `StatusCommandRunner`'s non-throwing continuation with
the signal number as its exit code, the classifier read that as "not signed in", and publishing it
*stamped the TTL* — so the wrong value suppressed its own repair for a full minute. The cost of a
missed guard is therefore a **wrong published value**, not merely a wasted probe. Two defences
landed with that fix and are what keeps the residual risk low: `CommandResult.signaled` (a killed
child is never mistaken for a CLI that ran and failed) and `GHAuthProbe.keepPrior` (a non-answer
neither writes nor stamps). The `withTimeout` gap below is a genuinely different mechanism and stays
deferred on its own merits.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -1
fix(macapp): stop a cancelled gh probe publishing "not signed in"

The PR panel intermittently claimed `GitHub CLI not signed in`, then
recovered about a minute later.

A superseded status sweep, or a workroom switched mid-probe, cancels the
task awaiting `gh auth status`. `StatusCommandRunner`'s `onCancel`
SIGKILLs the child, but its `withCheckedContinuation` is NON-throwing, so
`terminationHandler` still resumes with a normal-looking result: exit 9
(the signal number), `timedOut` false, and empty or half-written stdout.
`classifyGitHubCLI` fell through to its exit-code fallback and read that
as a logout, and `refreshGitHubCLI` published it — the one status mutation
buried inside an awaited function, where the callers' own
`Task.isCancelled` checks run too late to help.

Publishing it was half the bug. It also STAMPED `ghStatusCheckedAt`, so
the staleness gate turned every lane that would have healed the value into
an early return for a full minute: the wrong answer suppressing its own
repair, escapable only via the Refresh button's `force`.

Three changes, each independently tested:

- `CommandResult.signaled`, set from `terminationReason ==
  .uncaughtSignal`. `WorkroomCLI.CLIResult` has carried this exact field
  since a64e4269 ("stop 'exited with code 15' dialog on wake from
  sleep"); that fix never reached the runner that deliberately SIGKILLs
  on cancellation. Note `timedOut` implies `signaled` — the timeout path
  SIGTERMs — so consumers must test `timedOut` first.
- `GHAuthProbe`, so "the probe told us nothing" is representable. It was
  being collapsed into `.available`, which is not "no news" but a
  positive claim that erases a correct `.notAuthenticated` and leaves a
  silent panel with failing PR probes. `.keepPrior` mirrors
  `GHPreflight`/`CIResolution` and deliberately does not stamp the TTL,
  so the next lane re-probes instead of trusting a non-answer. This also
  fixes the pre-existing `.available`-on-timeout lie.
- `refreshGitHubCLI` checks `Task.isCancelled` before writing either the
  value or the stamp. A cancelled probe holds no fact at all.

Also: `VCSWriting`'s two failure classifiers rendered a signal number as
an exit status, so a `git push` SIGTERMed around sleep/wake showed the
literal "git exited 15" in the failure sheet — the very dialog a64e4269
set out to end. Only when stderr is empty, so a child that explained
itself keeps its real classification.

The `TODOS.md` entry deferring the `withTimeout` cancellation fix argued
it was safe because "every call site already checks `Task.isCancelled`".
That is the assumption this bug disproved; the rationale is corrected and
the (genuinely unrelated) deferral stands.

Measured against gh 2.97.0: `--json hosts` writes to stdout and exits 0
in every genuine state, including `{"hosts":{}}` when logged out. So a
non-zero exit means we learned nothing, not that you are logged out.

Verified by mutation: deleting the cancellation guard fails the new
regression test with exactly the reported symptom (`notAuthenticated`
published and the TTL stamped). 1985 tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

### `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` never reaches the `gh` auth probe (macapp) — gh-flap eng-review follow-up

**What:** decide whether `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (or another way of resolving gh's config dir) should reach
the NON-network `run` path that `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGitHubCLI` uses.

**Why:** `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` *is* in `StatusCommandRunner.forwardedAuthKeys`, but that allowlist is only
applied by `networkEnvironment`, i.e. behind `if network` in `run`. The gh auth probe is a plain `run`,
and the comment justifying the split says gh "carries its own token" — true, but gh FINDS that token via
its config dir. A user who sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` in `.zshrc` and launches from Finder therefore hands
gh a different config root than their terminal uses. Measured: an empty gh config dir returns
`{"hosts":{}}` on stdout with exit 0, which classifies as `.notAuthenticated` — a permanent false
"GitHub CLI not signed in" for someone who is signed in everywhere else. Same false claim the
cancelled-probe fix removed, reached by a completely different route.

**Pros:** closes the last known cause of a false "not signed in". **Cons:** widening the environment on
an automatic path is a deliberate, documented narrowness (`StatusCommandRunner` explains why a
wholesale transplant is refused for anything that runs without the user asking) — this is a security
posture question, not a one-line fix. A third allowlist ("non-secret, both paths") is probably the right
shape, and `GH_CONFIG_DIR` deserves the same thought.

**How to start:** `StatusCommandRunner.run`, where `if network` selects the environment. Decide the
allowlist question first, then apply to both paths.

**Depends on:** nothing.

**Priority:** P3 — real and measured, but it needs a policy decision, and the affected configuration is
uncommon.

### The other `CommandResult` consumers don't know about `signaled` (macapp) — gh-flap eng-review follow-up

**What:** consume `CommandResult.signaled` in `AgentRunner.classify`, `FileTreeModel`, and
`RustJJProvider.runCLI`.

**Why:** the gh-flap fix added `signaled` (a killed child reports its SIGNAL in `terminationStatus`, so
9 or 15 is not an exit code) and wired it into the gh classifiers plus both `CLIVCSWriter` failure
classifiers. Three consumers still read a raw exit code as evidence. `AgentRunner.classify` is the one
that reaches a user: a killed `claude` diagnosis becomes `.failed(exitCode: 9)` and the agent banner
shows "exit 9", which is exactly the class of nonsense commit `a64e4269` set out to end.
`FileTreeModel` gates on `result.ok`, so a signalled listing renders as a silently empty file tree.
`RustJJProvider` throws `VCSError.io("jj exited 9")`.

**Pros:** finishes the job — every place that reads an exit code as evidence learns that a signal is not
one. Each site is a one-line branch plus a test, since the mechanism already exists and is tested.
**Cons:** none of the three has a reported symptom, and two fail safe (an empty tree, a typed IO error)
rather than making a false claim.

**How to start:** `AgentRunner.classify` first (the only user-visible one): treat `signaled` as its own
outcome before the `exitCode != 0` branch, and mind that `timedOut` implies `signaled`, so the timeout
check must stay first.

**Depends on:** `CommandResult.signaled` (shipped).

**Priority:** P3 — cheap, but speculative until someone reports one.

### `ShellEnvironment` exposes no probe-readiness signal (macapp) — gh-flap eng-review follow-up

**What:** give `ShellEnvironment` a way for callers to know whether the interactive-shell PATH probe has
landed (or to await it), instead of silently degrading to the floor.

**Why:** `ShellEnvironment.path()` returns the probed PATH if the probe finished and the deterministic
floor otherwise, with nothing distinguishing the two. The probe is fired detached in `WorkroomApp.init`
and nothing joins it, while `refreshVCSToolReport` runs from `apply(projects)` — so a launch-time
`--version` probe can genuinely run against floor-only PATH. The floor covers Homebrew but not a
version-manager shim dir, Nix, or MacPorts, so those tools read as missing. `VCSToolVersionCache` no
longer *pins* such a verdict (it refuses to cache a discovered absence — shipped with the gh-flap work),
but that treats the symptom: any future caller reading `path()` early inherits the same ambiguity with
no way to detect it.

**Pros:** removes a whole class of "it depends when we asked" bugs, and would let the few callers that
genuinely need enrichment await it rather than guess. **Cons:** the probe is best-effort BY DESIGN — its
failures must degrade to the floor, never block — so a readiness signal must not become a hidden
dependency that stalls launch. Larger and more delicate than it first looks.

**How to start:** `ShellEnvironment.ProbeState` already tracks a generation; surface "has a probe
completed" from it, then audit `path()` callers for who should wait versus who should keep degrading.

**Depends on:** nothing.

**Priority:** P3 — the honest fix for a family of PATH-timing bugs, none currently reported.

fix(macapp): don't pin "jj isn't installed" from a launch-time PATH miss

`VCSToolVersionCache` cached every verdict for the whole process (`cached` is
cleared only by the tests-only `reset()`), including `.notInstalled`. That
verdict comes from exit 127 — the tool wasn't on PATH — and at launch the PATH
may still be the deterministic floor: `ShellEnvironment.path()` returns the
floor until the interactive-shell probe lands, the probe is fired detached in
`WorkroomApp.init` with nothing joining it, and `refreshVCSToolReport` runs from
`apply(projects)`. The floor covers Homebrew but not a version-manager shim dir,
Nix, or MacPorts — so a jj living in one read as missing, `warnings` showed
"jj isn't installed", and nothing could clear it short of a restart.

Cache only verdicts that aren't a discovered absence. Re-probing costs one
`--version`, and by then the enriched PATH has usually landed.

`probedJJ` is load-bearing in the new predicate: `probeJJ: false` reports jj
`.notInstalled` WITHOUT running anything, so counting that would refuse to cache
on every launch with no jj project and turn a one-shot `git --version` into one
per call. `.unknown` stays cacheable — `warnings` ignores it, so it never
becomes a false claim.

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -3 && git status --porcelain | head
feat(macapp): tell an old gh apart from a signed-out one, and share the probe

Three pieces of hardening on top of the cancelled-probe fix.

**`GitHubCLIStatus.tooOld`.** A gh older than 2.57 REJECTS `--active`/`--json`
rather than ignoring them — measured: exit 1, empty stdout, `unknown flag: --json`
on stderr — so it fell through to the exit-code fallback and reported a
perfectly signed-in user as permanently logged out, sending them to
`gh auth login`, which cannot fix a version problem. Detected on `unknown flag`
generically, since `--active` shares the floor and gh reports whichever flag it
parses first.

**Panel copy extracted and switched.** `ghWarning` decided title, body and
whether to show the install link from a chain of `status == .notInstalled`
ternaries, so every state that wasn't "not found" printed "not signed in" — the
new state would have inherited a message that misdirects. It is now a pure
`ghWarningCopy(for:)` with a case per state, unit-tested. It also carries an
a11y-identifier suffix, because every `staticTexts` element in this inspector's
tree reports an EMPTY label (measured): without an identifier a UI test can see
that some warning exists but never which one, which is useless for exactly the
regression worth catching. The identifier sits on the title rather than the
enclosing stack — combining the stack into one a11y element swallowed the
install link.

**`GitHubAuthCache`.** The gh verdict is a fact about the machine, but the
staleness check sat before the await and the stamp after it, while `AppStore` is
per-window and the verdict is a shared singleton — so two windows both probed
and the later write won. The cache now owns freshness and single-flight
outright, and the second owner of that truth (`ghStatusCheckedAt` plus its
`AppStore` proxy) is deleted.

Deliberately an INSTANCE, not the `static let shared` actor `VCSToolVersionCache`
uses for the same category of fact: `AppStore.init` documents that tests get a
fresh `ProjectStore`, and `make app-test` runs classes in parallel, so static
state would let one test's fake runner answer another's probe while `reset()`
cannot stop an in-flight task repopulating the cache. Its three previously
unwritten contracts are now written and tested: the probe runs in a
cache-owned task (a cancelled lane abandons the WAIT, not the answer), `force`
never joins a probe that predates the request (or Refresh silently wouldn't
refresh), and staleness is measured on a MONOTONIC clock so a backward wall-clock
step can't pin a verdict indefinitely. TTLs are injectable, so `.notAuthenticated`
gets its shorter 10s lease and the tests age verdicts in milliseconds.

**Fixture seam.** `refreshGitHubCLI` returns immediately in fixture mode — it
must, or a UI test would ask `gh` about the developer's own machine — so no test
could reach any warning state. `-WorkroomUITestGHStatus` seeds one, applied from
`seedFixtureStatuses` so it survives the manual Refresh that re-seeds.

2007 unit tests and 4 new XCUITests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
Done. Branch `fix/gh-auth-false-not-signed-in`, three commits, 20 files, working tree clean.

**The bug.** A superseded sweep or a workroom switched mid-probe SIGKILLs `gh auth status`. `StatusCommandRunner`'s `withCheckedContinuation` is non-throwing, so it still returned `exitCode: 9` with empty stdout, the classifier read that as a logout, and `refreshGitHubCLI` published it *and stamped the freshness clock* — so the wrong answer suppressed its own repair for 60s. Only Refresh escaped, which is why it "recovered itself".

**What landed**

`dda1dc2f` — the fix. `CommandResult.signaled`; `GHAuthProbe` so "no news" is representable (`.keepPrior` writes nothing *and* doesn't stamp); the `Task.isCancelled` guard. Also fixed `VCSWriting`'s two classifiers, which still rendered `git exited 15` in the failure sheet — the exact dialog `a64e4269` claimed to have ended, because that fix never reached this runner.

`6b29af15` — `VCSToolVersionCache` no longer pins a `.notInstalled` from a launch-time PATH miss.

`e4ae29bc` — `.tooOld` with an upgrade message; panel copy extracted to a tested pure function; `GitHubAuthCache` as the sole owner of freshness and single-flight, with its cancellation/force/monotonic-clock contracts written down; the fixture seam.

**Verified**: 2007 unit tests, 0 failures. 4 new XCUITests pass. `make app-lint` clean.

Two things I'd flag, both mid-task self-corrections worth knowing about:

- My first regression test was **green for the wrong reason** — the double returned the signalled shape, which `.keepPrior` already catches, so it would have passed with the guard deleted. Fixed to return a clean verdict, then **mutation-verified**: deleting the guard fails it with exactly the reported symptom (`notAuthenticated` published, clock stamped).
- Codex's review changed three of my own decisions. `.available` for a dead probe was a false positive that erases a true warning; a static single-flight actor would have broken the documented `AppStore()` test isolation under parallel runs; and bundling hurt revertability, hence the split.

**Not done**, so you know the gaps: I did not perform the manual before/after repro in the running app (the mutation test covers that guard more precisely, but it isn't the same as seeing it), and I ran only the new XCUITest class, not the full UI suite — the a11y identifier I added to the warning title is new surface in that tree.

Written and valid, but **it did not take effect in this session** — I retested `codex exec` sandboxed and it still fails with the same `Operation not permitted`. The sandbox config is a startup snapshot (you can see it fixed in my environment as a literal allowed-hosts/paths list), so a mid-session edit to `sandbox.*` isn't live.

What changed in `~/.claude/settings.json`:

```json
"permissions": { "allow": [ …, "Bash(codex exec:*)" ] },
"sandbox": { …, "excludedCommands": ["codex"] }
```

Why both: the allow rule only stops the *prompt*; `excludedCommands` is what stops the `EPERM`. Codex fails in-sandbox on two things unrelated to network — creating PATH aliases and starting its in-process app-server — so widening `allowWrite` wouldn't have helped, same as your `make app-*` case.

Scoped to `codex exec` rather than `codex:*` deliberately: gstack's outside voice and all three `/codex` modes go through `exec`, and every one passes `-s read-only`, so this doesn't blanket-approve a write-mode codex run.

Next session it should just work. If it still `EPERM`s, the `excludedCommands` match form is the thing to change — try `"codex exec"` instead of `"codex"`; the schema doesn't document whether it matches the first word or a command prefix, and I couldn't determine it without a restart. Either way the allow rule means the `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` fallback runs without prompting you.
